correctness.rationale: For a generic slice each face is determined by its minimal simplex-face support, a mixed subset of j+2 vertices; the binomial formula includes the empty cases. Centering and normalizing Gaussian coordinates gives the exact threshold bar G + c_n s_n with c_n=√n t_n. For deterministic bounded c_n the centered empirical count over the random O_P(n^{-1/2}) threshold displacement has fluctuation o_P(√n): on the n^{-3/4} grid the union bound costs O(n^{1/4}) and each count variance is O(√n); between grid points monotonicity or the binomial cell bound controls the remainder. Expanding s_n and the normal tail gives the two orthogonal Gaussian score projections and variance p(1−p)−φ²(1+c²/2)>0. The central face deficit uses the exact even binomial polynomial: its z² coefficient for z=K−n/2 is n^j/(2^j j!)+O_j(n^{j−1}), and the half-integer correction divided by n^{j+1} vanishes. The common scalar CLT then gives (1); ordinary Taylor gives (3), and in (2) the linear derivative is 2^{1−j}φ(0)c_n/j!+o(c_n), while the O_P(n^{j+1}) error is negligible precisely because nt_n→∞. K/n tends to an interior fraction, making empty slices negligible. These are proof checks, not reliance on the frozen simulation.
